newsitem.title: USA: Apple unveils new models, cuts prices.
newsitem.headline: Apple unveils new models, cuts prices.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc, filling in gaps in its consumer product lines, said it will sell two new models of Macintosh computers and will cut prices on some of its existing models by as much as 21 percent.

Apple said it will begin selling the entry-level Macintosh Performa 6360 next week for $1,499, a price comparable to entry-level personal computers based on Intel Corp microprocessors and running Microsoft Corp software.
The Performa 6360 features one of the Apple's fastest microprocessors, a CD-ROM drive and a modem, Apple said.

The company also plans to sell a new model with software that will let customers edit their home videos. The Macintosh Performa 6400/200, priced at $2,699, features a built-in video-editing program from Avid Technology Inc, a vendor of film production software.

Apple, which discontinued some of its Performa models this summer to cut marketing costs, said it will cut prices on its high-end Performa 6400 to $2,199 from $2,799, and a model with a slower microprocessor to $1,899 from $2,399.
Apple said the new models will meet the needs of families, small businesses and students.
